full_judgment:
Md Emdadul Huq J: Upon an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 1908 (shortly the Code, 1908), a rule was issued by this Court about- sustainability of the judgment and order dated 1-12-2015 by which the learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka (Deulia Bisoyok Adalot) dismissed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 102 of 2015 and thereby affirmed the Judgment and order dated 4-5-2015 passed by the Artharin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka (Executing Court) dismissing Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 2012 instituted under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code, 1908 and section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (shortly the Ain, 2003) for setting aside the auction sale, of some land in Artha Jari Case No.50 of 2906 pending before the Adalat. 

 2. After delivering the judgment; of dismissal, the Executing Court, by a separate order passed on the same day (4-5-2015), rejected an application earlier filed by the Petitioner (judgment debtor) under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code, 1908 for amendment of the original application of the said Miscellaneous Case. 

 3. By the 'Rule issuing' order dated' 13-3-2016 further proceeding of the said Artha Case was stayed by this Court. 

 Case of the Petitioner (Judgment debtor): The petitioner M/s Swdesh Poultry, represented by its proprietor, has stated that he obtained a loan of Taka 17,52,000 (Taka Seventeen lac Fifty Two thousand) from Krishi Bank, Uttara Branch (opposite party Nos. 1 and 2). The said Bank, as plaintiff, filed Artha Rin Suit No. 755 of 2004 and obtained an exparte decree dated 29-9-2005 for realization of an amount of Taka 28,94,383 (Taka Twenty Eight lac Ninety Four thousand three hundred Eighty three). Thereafter the decree holder bank filed Artha Jari Case No. 50 of 2006 for execution of the decree. 

 (a) paid Taka 10,20,295 to the Bank during pendency of Artha Jari case, on 'different dates  from 8-7-2009 to . 1-3-2010 (Annexure-L-series); 

 (b) deposited Taka 4,47,200 being the 50% of the remainder of the decreetal amount for filing Miscellaneous Appeal No.102 of 2015 to the learned District Judge against the order of dismissal of Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 2012 (Annexure-M); and 

 6. Petitioner has further stated that; in the Artha Jari Case the Executing Court put the mortgaged land to auction sale through court and five bidder submitted bids on 15-1-2012. The decree holder Bank filed a written objection to the effect that the said highest bid was lower than the actual price of the land. But the Executing Court, by order dated 17-1-2012, rejected the objection of the Bank and accepted the highest bid of Taka 38,00,000 for auction sale of the land measuring 11.56 decimals and directed the highest bidder to deposit the remaining price of the auction sale. In accepting the said highest bid, the Executing Court, relied on the purported Price List of 2012 of the concerned Sub-Registry office as filed by the bidder (vide-order-sheet Annexure-A). 

 7. On 26-1-2012, the judgment debtor (petitioner) appeared in the Artha Jari Case. He filed an application for staying further proceeding of the case and prayed payment of the remaining decreetal amount in three years. This application was not, however, decided and it was kept pending. 

 10. On 13-3-2012 the judgment debtor filed an application (Annexure-B) under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code, 1908 and section 57 of the Ain, 2003 for setting aside the auction sale. The said application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No.12 of 2012. In this application, he alleged inter alia that the auction price as quoted by the highest bidder was lower than the actual price and that fraud had been practised upon the court in the auction process by suppressing the actual price. He took another ground that he had already paid to the decree holder bank a considerable amount of the decreetal amount. 

 11. The decree holder bank and also the auction purchaser filed separate written objections (Annexure C and D). They contended inter alia that the auction sale had already been confirmed and that the Miscellaneous Case was barred by limitation as it was filed beyond the 'Specified period of limitation of 30 days. 

 12. The auction purchaser filed an application (Annexure-E) for rejection of the original application of the Miscellaneous Case under order 7 rule 11 Of the Code, 1908, on the ground inter alia that it was barred by limitation. Against this application the judgment debtor 

 13. During pendency of the Miscellaneous Case, the judgment debtor (petitioner), on 26-8-2014 filed an application under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code, 1908 for amendment of his original application (vide Annexure-G). However the Executing Court by order No. 110 dated 28-8-2014 (vide Annexure-H), kept the same pending. 

 14. The Executing Court fixed the Miscellaneous Case for peremptory hearing and after hearing all sides dismissed the Case by order dated 4-5-2015. This decision was affirmed by the appellate court by the impugned judgment, which is under challenge in this Revision. 

 15. Case of decree holder bank and the auction purchaser. In this Revision, opposite party Nos. 1 and 2, representing the decree holder Bank have filed a counter affidavit. The auction purchase (opposite party No. 3) has filed a separate but similar counter affidavit. 

 18. Deliberation in Revision: Mr Shafiullah with AKM Rabiul Hasan, the learned Advocates for the judgment debtor (petitioner), draw our attention to the photocopies of the bank receipts (Annexure-L-series and Annexure M and N) and submits that the judgment the debtor has paid more than 75% of the decreeetal amount during pendency of the Execution Case and the Miscellaneous Case and for the purpose of filing the Miscellaneous Appeal and this Revision. 

 22. Mr Shafiullah, next submits that the petitioner was not initially aware of the price fixed by the said Committee, but subsequently collected information about the same during pendency of the Artha Jari Case and informed the Executing Court by filing an application for amendment of the original application of the Miscellaneous Case containing specific reference to the price fixed by the said Committee but the Executing Court did not consider that application. 

 24. Mr Shafiullah lastly submits that although the application under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code, 1908 was filed after expiry of the prescribed period of limitation of 30 days, the settled principle of law is that fraud vitiates everything, that the limitation should not have been counted from 17-1-2017, being the date of acceptance of the bid but from the date of petitioner's knowledge and that the Executing Court should have considered petitioner's application for amendment should have been allowed after giving the parties an opportunity to prove their respective case with regard to the alleged fraud. 

 25. In support of his submission Mr Shafullah referrers to case of Abul Khair vs Abdul Latif Sardar reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167. 

 26. In reply Mr Md Shakhawat H. Khan, the learned Advocate for the decree holder Bank (opposite party Nos. 1 and 2) submits that the Miscellaneous Case was admittedly filed after the prescribed period of limitation of 30 days which is evidenced by the fact that the petitioner filed an application for condonation of the delay of 27 days and therefore the Executing Court lawfully dismissed the Misc. Case and this decision has been lawfully affirmed by appellate court. 

 28. The principal issue raised in this case is whether the Executing Court should have proceeded to admit evidence for determination of the issues of limitation and the alleged fraud with regard to the minimum price of the land as fixed by the relevant Committee of the Government compared to the price accepted in the auction sale. 

 29. The Rule issued in this case arose from the decision passed in a Miscellaneous Case under rule 90 of Order XXI of the Code, 1908. But in this Revision, the auction purchaser (opposite party No. 3) in his counter Affidavit has pleaded that the requirement of rule 89 of Order XXI has not been fulfilled. So these two rules should be examined first. 

 30. It is noted that section 33 of the Ain, 2003 does not contain the detailed provision for setting aside an auction sale. So, by virtue of section 6(1) of the Ain, 2003, the provisions of Order XXI, rule 89 and 90 of the Code, 1908 are applicable to an Artha Jari Case for the purpose of setting aside an auction sale held in execution of the decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. These two Rules are quoted below. 

 32. In the instant case, the judgment-debtor has taken the second option being the ground of the alleged fraud practiced upon the court. So the requirement of deposit of the decreetal dues and the compensation as prescribed by rule 89(1)(a) is not applicable to the present scenario. The plea taken by the auction purchaser in this Revision is not acceptable. 

 33. With regard to limitation, the order dated 1-4-2012 passed by the Executing Court in the order sheet of the Miscellaneous Case (vide order sheet Annexure) shows that the petitioner filed an application for condonation of the delay of 27 days in filing the case. However the Executing Court by order dated 19-4-2012, recorded a finding that since there was an allegation of fraud, the Case was maintainable and 'that' it would proceed. The Executing Court by the same order stayed further proceeding of the Artha Jari Case and kept the application for condonation of delay pending for further decision. The Miscellaneous Case proceeded to the PH stage and Executing Court by its order dated 4-5-2015 dismissed the Miscellaneous Case as being barred by limitation. 

 36. But, in the original application, filed on 13-3-2012 (Annexure-B) registered as Misc. Case No. 12 of 2012, in para-7-11, the Judgment debtor (petitioner) has generally taken the ground of fraud practised upon the court with regard to the Price of the land and also the ground of irregularity to the effect that the notice of auction sale was not duly in the news paper. Thereafter on 26-8-2014, he filed an application (Annexure-G) for amendment of the original application. In that application, he prayed for, inclusion of several new paragraphs 7(ka) to 7(Ja) and also the new paragraphs 10(ka) to 10(Gha). In the proposed new paragraphs 7(ka) to 7(ja) he was mostly stated the facts with regard to the proceeding of the Artha Jari Case. 

 38. In the same application (para-l6) he stated that the cause of action for filling the case on 12-3-2012 when he had come to from his lawyer about the issue of Certificate of Sale by the Court. 

 39. So, on the matter &limitation, an issue comes up as to on which date the cause of action of filing the Miscellaneous Case arose: The Executing Court, in its order dated 4-5-2015, counted the cause of action from 17-10-2012 which (Annexure-A) is quoted below: 

 41. In fact both the courts below failed to consider that an amendment application was made by the judgment debtor and it was pending. This is evident from the separate order passed by the Executing Court on 4-5-2015, after delivery of the Judgment i.e. on the same day dismissing the Miscellaneous Case. The rejection of an application for amendment of the original application is a judicial order, but, in the instant case it was done in a mechanical manner. It was passed at a time when the Executing Court had no jurisdiction to pass the order after disposing of the case. In that rejection order, the Executing Court recorded its decision as follows: 

 "As the Misc case is disallowed. So his petition is rejected (VOP)". 

 47. Our above view finds support in the observation and the principle laid down by the Appellate Division in the case of Abul Khair Mia vs Abdul Latif Sardar (32 DLR (AD) 167. In that case our Apex Court considered the issue of fraud in relation to service of summons of a suit in the background of an application for setting aside an exparte decree under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code, 1908. The Apex court observed as follows (underlines added): 

 49. The Executing Court passed an important Judicial order rejecting the application when it ceased to have jurisdiction over the case. Because on the same day it had earlier delivered the Judgment dismissing. 

 51. In the result, the rule is made absolute. The judgment and order dated 1-1-.2015 passed by the learned Additional District Judge (Deulia Bisoyok Adalot), Dhaka in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 102 of 2015 and the judgment and order dated 4-5-2015 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 2012 are hereby set aside. 

 52. The said Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 is directed to proceed with and to dispose of Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 2012 by way of first deciding the amendment application filed by Judgment debtor (petitioner). In deciding that application opposite parties should, be allowed a reasonable opportunity to file additional written objection, if any, If the amendment application is allowed the Adalat shall proceed to dispose of the Miscellaneous Case in accordance with law and in particular by allowing the parties to adduce evidence in support of their respective claim.
